Overview[ ]

Introduction[ ]

The ESP32-S3-Knob-Touch-LCD-1.8 is a high-performance, highly integrated microcontroller development board designed by Waveshare, featuring dual MCU control with ESP32-S3 and ESP32, integrated large capacity Flash and PSRAM, and a built-in 1.8inch LCD screen. It includes highly integrated audio decoding chip, rotary encoder, and other peripherals, enabling rapid development of intelligent voice AI applications.

Features[ ]

  • Equipped with dual MCUs (ESP32-S3 and ESP32), featuring up to 4 cores and a clock frequency up to 240 MHz
  • Supports 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi (802.11 b/g/n), Bluetooth 5 (BLE) and Classic Bluetooth, with onboard antenna
  • Built-in 512KB SRAM, 384KB ROM, 16MB Flash and 8MB PSRAM
  • Controls the touchscreen through the I2C interface, supporting interrupt output
  • Onboard audio decoding chip, microphone (MIC), rotary encoder, vibration motor, TF card slot, and battery charging management module
  • CNC precision-machined housing with aesthetic structure, sturdy and durable, and easy to carry

Development Tools[ ]

ESP32-S3-Knob-Touch-LCD-1.8 currently provides two development tools and frameworks, Arduino IDE and ESP-IDF, or you can use the bin file to flash directly. You can choose the appropriate development tool according to your project needs and personal habits.

Development Tools Description[ ]

Arduino IDE[ ]

Arduino IDE is an open source electronic prototyping platform, convenient and flexible, easy to get started. After a simple learning, you can start to develop quickly. At the same time, Arduino has a large global user community, providing an abundance of open source code, project examples and tutorials, as well as rich library resources, encapsulating complex functions, allowing developers to quickly implement various functions.

ESP-IDF[ ]

ESP-IDF, or full name Espressif IDE, is a professional development framework introduced by Espressif Technology for the ESP series chips. It is developed using the C language, including a compiler, debugger, and flashing tool, etc., and can be developed via the command lines or through an integrated development environment (such as Visual Studio Code with the Espressif IDF plugin). The plugin offers features such as code navigation, project management, and debugging, etc.


These two development tools each have their own advantages, and developers can choose according to their own needs. For beginners, we also provide bin files for flashing, making development simpler.

01_ADC_Test[ ]

Demo description

Code analysis

  • adc_bsp_init(void) : Initializes ADC1, including creating an ADC one-time trigger unit and configuring channel 0 for ADC1.
  • adc_get_value(float *value,int *data) : Reads the value of ADC1 channel 0 and calculates the corresponding voltage value based on the reference voltage and resolution, stores it at the position where the incoming pointer points to, and stores 0 if the read fails.
  • adc_example(void* parameter): Initialize ADC1 and then create an ADC task that reads the ADC value every 1 second and calculates the system's voltage based on the raw ADC value.

    • The purpose of CmakeLists.txt: When compiling ESP-IDF, the build tool CMake first reads the content of the top-level CMakeLists.txt in the project directory to read the build rules and identify the content to be compiled. FAQ[ ]

Question: Why can't the program be flashed?

 Answer:

This product features two onboard chips, ESP32-S3 and ESP32. The two insertion orientations of the Type-C plug connect to different download channels.

  • If programming fails, the serial port is not found, or the connection cannot be established, please perform the following steps first:
    • 1. Disconnect the Type-C cable;
    • 2. Flip the Type-C plug 180°;
    • 3. Re-insert the cable and attempt programming again.

Question: Failed to set up the VSCode environment?

Question: Error when compiling an Arduino program?

 Answer:

Question: What should I do if I can't find the AppData folder?

 Answer:
  • Some AppData folders are hidden by default and can be set to show.
  • English system: Explorer->View->Check "Hidden items"
  • Chinese system: File Explorer -> View -> Display -> Check "Hidden Items"


Question: How do I check the COM port I use?

 Answer:
  • Windows system:

①View through Device Manager: Press the Windows + R keys to open the "Run" dialog box; input devmgmt.msc and press Enter to open the Device Manager; expand the "Ports (COM and LPT)" section, where all COM ports and their current statuses will be listed.
②Use the command prompt to view: Open the Command Prompt (CMD), enter the "mode" command, which will display status information for all COM ports.
③Check hardware connections: If you have already connected external devices to the COM port, the device usually occupies a port number, which can be determined by checking the connected hardware.

  • Linux system:

①Use the dmesg command to view: Open the terminal.
①Use the ls command to view: Enter ls /dev/ttyS* or ls /dev/ttyUSB* to list all serial port devices.
③Use the setserial command to view: Enter setserial -g /dev/ttyS* to view the configuration information of all serial port devices.


Question: Why does the program flashing fail when using a MAC device?

 Answer:
  • Install MAC Driver and flash again.

=BIN File Flashing=
*Download the BIN files we provided under [[#BIN File | BIN File]] in advance. Below, an example will be given for the Windows system; other systems are similar
1. Extract the downloaded BIN file compressed file, press and hold WIN+R ->enter CMD and enter Enter to enter the command line, and then check whether the system has Python and pip (most computers will have), as shown in the figure:
[[File:ESP32-S3-Knob-Touch-LCD-1.8-22.png|1000px]]
You can see that the Python version is 3.11.9 and the pip version is 24.0 If there are no corresponding versions, you can visit the Python official website to install Python first. After installation is successful, install pip using the command line 
curl https://bootstrap.pypa.io/get-pip.py -o get-pip.py
2. Install the esptool tool as shown in the figure:
[[File:ESP32-S3-Knob-Touch-LCD-1.8-23.png|1000px]]
Enter the command above to install esptool You can see that the system already has ESPTOOL version 24.0 3. Check the path of the esptool tool, as shown in the figure:
[[File:ESP32-S3-Knob-Touch-LCD-1.8-24.png|1000px]]
Enter the command above to view the original path of esptool 4. Add the path to the user environment variable, and then reopen the command line, as shown in the figure:
[[File:ESP32-S3-Knob-Touch-LCD-1.8-25.png|1000px]]
5. The board has two MCUs, ESP32 and ESP32-S3. We first identify which board the COMx connected to the computer is, as shown in the figure:
[[File:ESP32-S3-Knob-Touch-LCD-1.8-50.png|1000px]] 1. Enter the command : esptool.exe --port COMx --baud 115200 chip_id 2. COMx refers to the COM after the device is connected to the computer, which can be checked through the Device Manager 3. Confirm that it is ESP32 or ESP32S3, you can check the chip type 6. The board has two MCUs onboard, namely ESP32 and ESP32S3. First, flash the bin file to the ESP32, as shown in the image:
[[File:ESP32-S3-Knob-Touch-LCD-1.8-26.png|1000px]]
1. --chip esp32: Indicates the chip type, such as ESP32, ESP32S3, ESP32C6, etc. 2. --port: Indicates the serial port, which can be checked in the Device Manager -> Ports to see the corresponding COMx 3. --baud: Baud rate 4. write_flash: Flashing command 5. -z: Enables compression 6. 0x0: Flashing address 7. .bin: Indicates the firmware path, which is the path of the firmware after decompression If the flashing fails, check whether the chip type and COMx are incorrect, reconfirm and execute the flashing command 7. Next, flash the ESP32-S3 bin file, as shown in the figure:
[[File:ESP32-S3-Knob-Touch-LCD-1.8-27.png|1000px]]
1. Note that it needs to be changed to ESP32S3 2. COM also needs to be modified to the corresponding one 3. Be careful not to select the wrong BIN file If the flashing fails, check whether the chip type and COMx are incorrect, reconfirm and execute the flashing command 8. After flashing is complete, toggle the switch to reboot the device, as shown in the image:
[[File:675px-ESP32-S3-Knob-Touch-LCD-1.8-21.png|450px]]
